assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a single microwave photon and a single superconducting artificial atom interact in the strong-coupling regime on a chip, with controllable, measurable quantum behaviour. It is the architecture behind dispersive readout, the transmon and most superconducting quantum processors, and it opened circuit and waveguide quantum optics as a new regime of physics. This is the clean basic-physics-to-enabling-platform case I weigh most, and it also underlies the dynamical Casimir and giant-atom work I know first hand.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal by Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf and the Yale and ETH experiments are the decisive work. The supplied credited names omit Andreas Wallraff, whose first strong-coupling experiment is arguably decisive, so this three-person configuration leaves a gap I cannot fix within the allowed names. Schoelkopf (experiment and the transmon), Girvin (theory) and Blais (theory) are the best supported subset. Blais is a younger theorist, and it is a fair question whether Wallraff would be more deserving than he is.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across many independent laboratories for about two decades, and the interpretation is stable. Timing is good; the 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, which is a separate and earlier discovery, so there is a mild question of whether the committee wants superconducting circuits again so soon.
uncertainties: Wallraff is not among the credited names, so credit may be incomplete.
Whether the committee would follow the 2025 circuits prize with a second superconducting-circuit award so soon.
My close ties to this field are a possible conflict of interest and bias in favour of this candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned strongly correlated many-body physics into a controllable laboratory system: the Mott-insulator transition, single-site microscopy and programmable Hubbard models. The result is original, clear and has changed how many-body quantum physics is studied. It is also a mature quantum-simulation platform.
assessment.attribution: The credit is spread over the Jaksch-Zoller proposal, Greiner and Bloch's Mott transition, Esslinger's fermion work and Cirac and Zoller's theory. Five names are credited and only three may be chosen. Bloch, Greiner and Zoller give a balanced experiment-plus-theory trio, but Esslinger and Cirac have strong claims and a three-person prize leaves real allocation disputes.
assessment.maturity: Well established across many groups for more than twenty years, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Several equally strong claimants for three places.
Overlap with the Cirac and Zoller theory candidate and with Rydberg-array quantum simulation, so the discovery boundary is fuzzy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the HgTe edge-state transport observation, opened an entire field of topological band theory. It is conceptually original and led to Dirac and Weyl materials and many materials discoveries. It is somewhat outside my own area, so I defer partly to colleagues in condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical predictions. Molenkamp's group made the key experimental observation in HgTe (with Zhang, Bernevig and Hughes predicting the HgTe case; those theorists are not credited, so some credit is unresolved). The three-person configuration is plausible and fairly clean.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by ARPES and transport in several materials, and the framework is stable. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe prediction and Fu, Kane and Mele's three-dimensional work make credit boundaries contestable.
I would defer to condensed-matter colleagues on the relative weight of theory and experiment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reached 10^-18 fractional precision and opened the way to a redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. The measurement is clean and each systematic effect can be traced to a physical detail. I find this very appealing.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice and Ye led the highest-precision realisations and the comparison work. A two-person prize is clean, though Hall and Hänsch (already recognised in 2005) and the ion-clock community, in particular Wineland's group, were relevant to the broader precision story.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several independent laboratories, with international comparisons. Recognition is timely, and the redefinition of the second is still pending.
uncertainties: Overlap with trapped-ion clocks, whose recognition came in 2012.
Whether the committee sees this as improved precision rather than a new discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and was a landmark of large-scale experiment. The theorists were recognised in 2013, so the experimental side is an obvious gap. Particle physics is outside my own expertise, so I rely on colleagues for the fine judgement.
assessment.attribution: A prize to collaborations of thousands is hard to attribute. Gianotti (ATLAS spokesperson at the discovery), Jenni (ATLAS founder) and Della Negra (CMS founder) are proposed, and Virdee has an equally strong claim. The selection of individuals will be contested because the statutes limit the prize to three people.
assessment.maturity: The result is confirmed by two independent experiments and by Run 2 measurements of the couplings; the discovery is mature.
uncertainties: No fair way to credit a collaboration of this size, and the choice among four credited names is arbitrary.
The relation to the separate LHC conception candidate (B029) is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened a new class of tunable quantum matter. It is a striking, original result that spawned moiré physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald's 2011 theory and Jarillo-Herrero's 2018 experiments are the central pieces. The Cao et al. first author is not credited, which leaves credit questions. The three-person configuration is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely, but the interpretation of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still evolving, so I think it is a little early.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity is still debated.
Prize timing could be premature relative to older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error-correcting codes and the threshold theorem for fault-tolerant computation are the theoretical basis for any large-scale quantum computer, and I think they matter greatly for the field I work in. The ideas are original and deep.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane introduced the first codes, and Kitaev the topological codes and fault-tolerant ideas. Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme and Aharonov and Ben-Or are other claimants, which makes a three-person selection hard to defend.
assessment.maturity: The theory is established, but experiments with logical qubits are only beginning to demonstrate below-threshold operation, and full-scale error correction is still ahead. I would call it premature to prize it now. The prize rewards a discovery and not a technology promise.
uncertainties: Whether it counts as physics rather than computer science or mathematics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Loss-DiVincenzo proposal for spin qubits in quantum dots and the experimental control of single and coupled spins showed a route to silicon-compatible qubits, with recent high-fidelity operation. It is a significant conceptual and technical contribution.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo proposed the scheme, and Vandersypen leads in experimental demonstration (alongside other groups, such as Kouwenhoven's, which are not credited). The three-person configuration is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation by many groups and now silicon platforms with good fidelity. It is still developing, so I rank it behind more mature candidates.
uncertainties: Maturity: scaling is not yet demonstrated.
